title: LOW-COST RESILIENT SOFTWARE DEFINED RADIO PLATFORM FOR SATELLITE APPLICATIONS
description: The evolution of SDR platforms is enabling the use of general-purpose hardware for various application, allowing hardware reuse andcost reduction, and enabling "niche" applications at rather low cost. The SDRs rapidly moved from research applications to widespread applications, including space missions. However, SDRs do not yet address well cybersecurity.The proposed concept aims at enhancing cybersecurity of SDR platforms with the components and the barriers required, enabling their use in applications where the device can be subject to tampering. The proposed technology shall extend to cybersecurity the concept of SDR itself, where the user doesnot need to design hardware but just software, allowing the user to access secure platform without need for designing it. The integration of a secure element (e.g. crypto-processor or SIM card) will protect the cryptographic material from tampering and leakage. This will remove the need for expensive security modules for applications relying on symmetric key cryptography, and protect the stored public key certificates from tampering. Moreover, easing the access to validated crypto functions implemented in hardware will also reduce the risk of cyberattacks exploiting faulty implementations of cryptographic functions.Beside the secure processors, thewhole platform integrating the SDR shall be designed to prevent cyberattacks. This includes, but is not limited to, secure attestation of the components, sensors and controlled latency in the communication buses inside the platform. Specific care shall also be devoted to the secure software update, in order to prevent unintended manipulation of the software from third party, increasing flexibility by SDR functions, performance upgrade.Additionally, high quality RF frontend, for instance with low phase noise, may enable security-oriented signal processing techniques, such as RF fingerprinting. Such capabilities could reduce time-to-market and significantly ease adoption of those satellite specific features by a wider user community enhancing the cybersecurity. Beforehand, it needs to reach a TRL high enough prior to its adoption by the industry, therefore, the activity will aim the development of a breadboard and then demonstrate its capabilities for several use cases to be consolidated in the frame of the activity (e.g. Satcom, GNSS,etc.). The design shall also be future-proof, covering VHF to C-band, which encompass most of the satellite bands associated to handheld or mobile devices.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Consolidation of use cases and derivation of the requirements and candidate architectures. Development and integration of the hardware. Development of the software features enabling the different selected use cases (software drivers and applications). Validation process with field trials.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: ULTRA LOW POWER CONSUMPTION MICROCONTROLLER FOR DEEP SPACE HIBERNATION SYSTEMS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop an ultra-low power, Mixed Signal Microcontroller (MCU) for hibernation control for Avionics units.Description: Planetary and deep space missions necessitate a hibernation controller that can operate reliably at low power for extended periods, even under extreme temperature variations. This controller is essential for managing the wake-up and shut-down processes of avionics during planetary nights and deep space travel, ensuring the spacecraft's survival and functionality throughout the mission. Recent advancements in semiconductor technology and manufacturing have significantly reduced the power consumption of digital logic andprocessors, while also expanding their operating temperature range to include cryogenic levels. These developments are particularlyrelevant for ensuring the reliable operation of Mixed Signal Microcontrollers (MCUs) across a wide temperature spectrum at ultra-low power levels. MCUs, commonly used as primary processing units in control applications and on-board computers, can be equipped withsmall dedicated circuits to enter hibernation mode and wake up periodically for operational tasks or in response to sensor alarms. This results in power consumption as low as 10 nA. An MCU with such capabilities would be ideal for the hibernation controller in avionics subsystems, offering significant advantages over discrete solutions with limited functionality and higher power consumption. Theactivity includes a survey of available space-grade MCUs to identify a suitable candidate for managing the hibernation and control of the start-up and shut-down processes of avionics electronics. The final selection is based on a thorough analysis and environmental testing of the identified MCU. Integrating a small, ultra-low power, reliable clock and monitoring alarm circuit are used to upgrade the selected MCU to serve as a hibernation controller for planetary and deep space missions. The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Use case determination - Analysis, thermal environmental testing and selection of space grade MCUs for hibernation controller functions - Evaluation of the MCU technology for the implementation of an ultra-low power clock and monitoring alarm circuit - Design of the ultra low-power hibernation clock and monitoring alarm function - Incorporation of the hibernation clock and monitoring alarm into the MCU - Manufacturing of the hibernation MCU (h-MCU) - Thermal environmental testing of the h-MCU - Evaluation of MCU and hibernation functions - Demonstration of an h-MCU module for incorporation into space avionic systems.ProcurementPolicy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
